search_parameters.q: What did the latest US Federal Reserve meeting decide about interest rates?

text_blocks.snippet: At its latest meeting on September 16, 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
snippet_highlighted_words: raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent

list.snippet: Target Range: Increased by 25 basis points (1/4 percentage point) to 3.75% – 4.00%.
Vote Tally: Approved by a unanimous 12–0 vote.
Reserve Balances: The Board of Governors voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90%, effective September 17, 2026.
Primary Credit Rate: Approved a 1/4 percentage point increase to 4.0%, effective September 17, 2026.
Economic Activity: Expanding at a solid pace with resilient domestic spending and robust capital investment.
Labor Market: Job gains have kept pace with the growing workforce.
